calls.reason: The only evidence is RBC's March 2024 note, which calls valuations stretched but says the market is not a repeat of the tech bubble. One adviser's view does not settle whether Q1 2024 was an AI bubble.

This is a hedged, undated conditional forecast. Nothing shows the profit failure it depends on has happened. Nvidia's mid-2026 revenue kept growing, and the Revenera survey shows only margin pressure on software providers.
Pew and OpenAI data show heavy chatbot use and some change in how people search. But the claim sets no deadline or threshold, and nothing ties these trends to a clear breakthrough after April 2024.

Epoch projects human text could run out between 2026 and 2032 and calls synthetic-data results mixed. Gerstgrasser finds that keeping real data alongside synthetic data avoids collapse. The evidence does not settle the claim either way.

Schneider and CBRE show real cooling and power pressures in early 2024. Schneider also presents liquid cooling as a workable fix, so nothing shows these limits were stopping AI progress. The 'mediocre' part is opinion.

XPS and FT reporting both say Q1 2024 was global equities' best first quarter since 2019 and credit AI enthusiasm as a major driver, alongside other factors. The 'hype cycle' part is his stated fear, not a fact claim.
